clue.text: Bill joins Bill or retired performer

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill to be paid

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the bill and 'or' are read backwards together

parts.note: a tab is a bill run up at a bar
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two men called Bill team up with a performer who has given up the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns the second bill and 'or' backwards as one run; 'joins' is just the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbling, balancing circus artist is a kind of performer.

clue.text: Trigger-happy types will soon be out of this rindless bacon

definitions.text: Trigger-happy types will soon be out of this

indicators.note: rindless means with its outer skin taken off, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: gammon is cured bacon from the hind leg

explanation.surface: Gun-crazy people are about to run out of lean bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rindless' strips the first and last letters from GAMMON.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammunition is what quick-firing gun users run out of, and this is its slang short form.

clue.text: Prince is not shut up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ajar means slightly open, not shut

explanation.surface: A royal heir refuses to keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses AJAR in this down entry. 'is' is a link; 'shut up' looks like be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A raja is an Indian prince or king.

clue.text: Garrison Keillor's last artist between supports

indicators.note: between puts the letter and the artist inside the supports

parts.note: to back is to support, so backs means supports

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the American author's name

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Garrison Keillor's latest painter stands between the props.
explanation.walkthrough: Garrison Keillor is the American radio humorist; his first name is the definition, and 'between' sets his last letter and the artist inside the supports.
explanation.definitionFit: Barracks are the buildings housing soldiers, and a garrison is troops stationed in a place.

clue.text: Minority Africans express disapproval with European agreement

parts.note: to tut is to click the tongue in disapproval
si is yes in Spanish and Italian

explanation.surface: Tongue-clicking over a European treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are a people of Rwanda and Burundi, the smaller group beside the Hutu majority.

clue.text: Beetle vehicle fits into more up-market vehicle if one gets out

indicators.note: fits into means the first vehicle goes inside the second
one of the two identical letters in the car's name leaves, as a passenger gets out

parts.note: a Saab is a Swedish car, pricier than a VW Beetle
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A VW Beetle squeezes into a posher car once a passenger climbs out.
explanation.walkthrough: Beetle looks like the Volkswagen but is the insect; 'if one gets out' removes just one of the Swedish car's two As before 'fits into' does its work.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle held sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Poet's honour, without impediment, on the up

indicators.note: without means outside, so the honour surrounds the turned impediment

parts.note: CBE is Commander of the Order of the British Empire, an honour

indicators.note: on the up in a down clue means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a bar is an obstacle or impediment

explanation.surface: A poet's award comes once barriers to advancement are removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the up' turns only the impediment, and 'without' (outside) wraps the honour round it. 'Poet's' gives the definition plus 's for is.
explanation.definitionFit: George Crabbe was an English poet, author of The Borough.

clue.text: Thought of doing it with Florence

indicators.note: doing in the sense of working over or redoing, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone imagines having a fling with a woman called Florence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing' mixes IT and FLORENCE together. 'of' and 'with' are links; 'doing it' looks like sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful thought or contemplation is called reflection.

clue.text: Cilla's without the words — so someone's got in hers?

indicators.note: without means outside, so the singer's name goes round the words

parts.note: Cilla Black was a British singer and TV host; her surname with the S
the book of a musical is its script, its spoken words

explanation.surface: Cilla Black has lost her lyrics, so someone must be out of favour with her.
explanation.walkthrough: Cilla Black was a British singer and Blind Date host, and 'without' sets the words inside her name. To be in someone's black books is to be out of their favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of favour with someone is an idiom described as being in their bad records.

clue.text: Old PM, personal appeal unknown, once reached at 28 19

parts.note: John Major was British Prime Minister 1990 to 1997
'it' is old slang for sex appeal or personal magnetism
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A former prime minister, lacking charisma, once came of age at a certain number.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 19 reads as the numbers entered there, twenty-one: until 1970 British adulthood began at 21.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal adulthood is called coming of age or reaching one's majority, formerly at twenty-one in Britain.

clue.text: Fibre plastic fair chokes a fellow

indicators.note: chokes means grips round the throat, so the rearranged letters hold the other pair inside
plastic means pliable or mouldable, so the letters of fair are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

explanation.surface: A plastic fibre at a funfair is strangling some poor chap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic' turns FAIR into RFIA; 'chokes' puts A + F inside it after the R. Plastic looks like the material of the fibre but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffia is a natural fibre from palm leaves, used for weaving and tying.

clue.text: Sweet Matt left off moving etc

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the letter for left leaves

parts.note: matt means dull, without shine

indicators.note: moving means shifting about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Matt sweetly leaves after shifting some miscellany around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' takes L from DULL, leaving DUL; 'moving' turns ETC into CET. Matt looks like a name but is a finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dulcet means sweet and pleasant, as in dulcet tones.

clue.text: Ankle-length garment taken on quiet holiday for potter's 19 24 23

parts.note: a maxi is a long skirt or dress reaching the ankles
mum means silent, as in keep mum
a break is a short holiday

explanation.surface: A long dress is packed for a peaceful getaway by a ceramics artist.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker a potter pockets balls, and 19 24 23 read as their entries give one-four-seven, 147, the top score from one visit. 'taken on' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker, the highest possible single-visit score of 147 is called the perfect clearance or top break.

clue.text: Where a clown's oversized shoes were made eventually?

definitions.text: Where a clown's oversized shoes were made
definitions.meaning: a cobbler shapes shoes on a last, and a clown's huge shoes would need an extended one

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for finally, and literally a cobbler's lengthy shoe form.

clue.text: Odds that would make a wage slave's day?

definitions.text: Odds that would make a wage slave's day?

parts.words: Odds that would make a wage slave's day?
parts.note: betting odds written as two numbers with 'to' between double as the standard office working hours

explanation.definitionFit: Office working hours, starting at nine and ending at five, describe a wage slave's day.

clue.text: Messing about with kitchen hard going: decide not to

indicators.note: messing about means fiddling around with, so the letters are jumbled
going means leaving, so the hard letter departs from the jumbled pool

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Fooling around in the kitchen proves so tough that someone abandons the plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Messing about' rearranges WITH KITCHEN, and 'going' takes out its H (hard) before the rest is arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsider and so refrain from an action is an idiom for pausing to reflect again.

clue.text: Heavy object with 17 and 24's product

parts.note: multiplying the numbers entered at those two lights gives eight

explanation.surface: A heavy item turns out to be the result of multiplying two numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 17 and 24 as the numbers their entries spell, then multiply them.
explanation.definitionFit: A weight is a heavy object, such as a paperweight or a gym weight.

clue.text: See 19
Ruthlessly determined underworld criminal

parts.note: hell is the underworld of the dead
bent is slang for crooked or criminal

explanation.surface: A gangster from the underworld is ruthless in pursuit of his aims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' as criminal is British slang, as in a bent copper.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell-bent means recklessly set on doing something whatever the cost.

clue.text: Footballing combination went out in unexciting draw?

indicators.note: in means placed inside the two letters

parts.note: a goalless match ends nil-nil

indicators.note: out means wrong or awry, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A football team's move came to nothing in a dull goalless match.
explanation.walkthrough: A goalless 0-0 draw supplies the two outer letters; 'out' rearranges the verb and 'in' sets it between them.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, a quick pass and return pass between two teammates is this named passing move.

clue.text: State capital producing jam without litter all over the place

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the jam word surrounds the jumble

parts.note: to jam a mechanism is to lock it fast

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A capital city makes preserves without any rubbish scattered around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' gives ITTLER, and 'without' (outside) has the jam word wrap it after its first letter. 'producing' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Rock is the capital city of the US state of Arkansas.

clue.text: Save, without displeasure, bottom to top, divided capital

indicators.note: without means outside, so the save word goes round the other

parts.note: but means except, as save does

indicators.note: in a down entry, the bottom letter of the word is moved up to its top

parts.note: ire is anger or displeasure

explanation.surface: Rescue a war-split capital city, sparing it further anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom to top' moves the last letter of the anger word up front, making EIR; 'without' (outside) wraps the save word round it. Beirut was split by a Green Line in Lebanon's civil war.
explanation.definitionFit: Beirut, Lebanon's capital, was partitioned into east and west during the civil war.

clue.text: Prickly plant makes Shakespearean theatre the thing here — "let's off"

parts.note: the Globe was the London playhouse where Shakespeare's company performed
this means the thing here, as against that over there

indicators.note: off means awry or not right, so those letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word let, with the 's read as is

explanation.surface: A spiky weed becomes the star of Shakespeare's playhouse, so someone suggests leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let's off' is read as 'let is off': 'off' rearranges LET into TLE, which ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe thistle, Echinops, is a spiky plant with round blue flower heads.

clue.text: See 28
See 28
I say "source"

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of surprise, like goodness or my
a spring or wellspring, the source of water

explanation.definitionFit: The same word is both an interjection of surprise and a spring that supplies water.

clue.text: Independent article inside: "A peep into buzzer housing"

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: inside means the independent-article pair goes within the other pieces

parts.note: to pry is to peep nosily into something
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper story invites a peek into a doorbell's casing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' places I + A within A PRY, after its P. Buzzer looks like a doorbell but means a bee; housing means home.
explanation.definitionFit: An apiary is a place where beehives are kept, home to buzzing insects.

clue.text: Here winter sports ace gets to compete to a greater degree

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards
to vie is to compete
more means to a greater extent

explanation.surface: A champion skier sets out to compete harder at the slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: AVIEMORE is a ski resort in the Scottish Highlands near the Cairngorms. 'gets to' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: This Highland town is Scotland's best-known ski resort, a venue for snow sports.

clue.text: Top-of-the-board boat crews getting level all the time

parts.note: on a dartboard the number at the top is twenty
... are rowing boats with crews of ... oarsmen
even means level or flat

explanation.surface: Champion rowing crews pulling level with each other throughout the race.
explanation.walkthrough: Darts boards put 20 at the top. 'getting' is the link. The answer is written in figures as 24/7.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week, is an idiom for constantly or continuously.

clue.text: Illegitimate person born with a particular skill

definitions.meaning: an old term for a child born out of wedlock is a ... child

definitions.text: person born with a particular skill
definitions.meaning: someone with an innate gift is called a born talent or a ...

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both an old euphemism for born outside marriage and a gifted natural talent.
